A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, support reliable comparison despite substantial restructuring.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-classification membership-inference experiments, synthetic simulations, regression results and individual-sample analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original image-classification and regression results and adds RMIA evaluations and numerical analyses of the simplified model.

M1.justification: The proposed regression predictor remains log10(TPR−FPR) regressed on log10(S) and log10(C), with unchanged Head/FiLM configurations and simplified Gaussian class-mean classifier. RMIA is an added existing attack, while the new vulnerability formulas are theoretical derivations.

E1.justification: Both versions use Patch Camelyon, CIFAR10, EuroSAT, Pets, Resics45 and CIFAR100, alongside simplified Gaussian-class data. The new RMIA evaluations and simulations retain the same membership-inference task and represented domains.

E2.justification: v3 adds RMIA (Zarifzadeh et al., 2024) alongside LiRA in Figure 2 and Figures A.6–A.8. This substantially expands the principal attack comparison from one attack to two across the retained image benchmarks.

E3.justification: v2's individual-sample protocols using percentile bins, training deciles and nearest-neighbor distances are removed. v3 adds RMIA evaluation and a bound-check simulation specifying five targets, 100000 z samples and 1000 t samples (Table A1). Overview plots switch from TPR to TPR−FPR; retained training splits, tuning budgets and hyperparameter ranges are unchanged.

E4.justification: v3 removes the gradient-norm, training-stage and feature-distance analyses from v2 Section 5 and Appendix B.5, plus the earlier synthetic distribution-statistic diagnostics. It adds cross-attack prediction checks, numerical RMIA bound-gap checks and small-FPR approximation analysis (Figure A.7, Table A1 and Appendix D). The alternative regression analysis is retained.

E5.justification: Six-seed shot sweeps, twelve-seed class sweeps, Clopper–Pearson intervals and regression confidence intervals are retained. However, v3 Figure A.7 newly summarizes RMIA prediction-check results using the highest TPR over six seeds, whereas the retained prediction plots use medians.

E6.justification: The retained numerical tables match: v2 Tables A3–A9 correspond to v3 Tables A4–A10, including regression R2 values 0.930 and 0.790 at FPR=0.001. v3 adds RMIA results showing a similar power-law trend but greater low-FPR instability, plus new simulation and approximation results. Individual-gradient, distance and earlier synthetic diagnostic results are removed.

T1.justification: v3 replaces the shorter LiRA asymptotic argument with location-scale per-example lemmas, an explicit LiRA vulnerability expression, RMIA upper bounds and average-case corollaries. Appendices A–D add extensive derivations, shared-variance justification, relaxed distribution-knowledge assumptions, proofs and approximation analysis.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions shift from an empirical LiRA study with gradient-based individual vulnerability findings toward theoretical and empirical analysis of two attacks. The gradient-predictiveness contribution disappears; per-example vulnerability formulas and LiRA/RMIA power-law contributions become central. The dataset-level regression claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 attributes the low-FPR slope discrepancy to missing distributional details; v3 offers a specific small-S approximation explanation supported by Appendix D. v3 also adds qualifications about distribution knowledge, bounded-distance worst-case interpretations and memorization, while removing interpretations of gradient norms, training stages and feature distances.

D1.justification: v3 explains the existing LiRA shadow-model reuse procedure more explicitly. Most model, hyperparameter, hardware and dataset-access details are retained. Opacus gradient-recording details and the promise of an open code repository after acceptance disappear; both versions still state that reproduction code is supplied as supplementary material.

R1.justification: v3 adds RMIA, Aerni and Leemann on individual vulnerability, and Feldman and Zhang on memorization. References supporting individual DP accounting and Opacus disappear with the removed sample analysis. These are focused changes around the revised emphasis rather than a wholesale replacement of the prior-work discussion.

P1.justification: The abstract and contribution narrative are substantially rewritten, theory precedes empirical evaluation, the individual-sample section is removed, and the appendices are reorganized into A–F. The title, author block and section styling also change.

P2.justification: Figure 1 and supplementary dataset-property plots are redrawn using TPR−FPR, with revised axes and legends. New RMIA plots, a bound-check table and an approximation figure replace substantial earlier simulation and individual-sample displays. Retained prediction figures and tables are relocated and renumbered, alongside a changed document template.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful cross-attack evidence, clearer assumptions and a concrete explanation of the earlier low-FPR discrepancy. However, it removes the substantial individual-sample empirical study, and its new RMIA power-law proof relies on a bound-gap ordering supported only numerically (Appendix C.4/Table A1: five targets, with reported instability). These gains and unresolved support gaps leave the net quality direction uncertain.
